title: One Coffee Ad Three Shapes
tests: Produces three genuinely adapted aspect-ratio variants of one cohesive ad rather than unrelated designs or cropped copies.

exact_text.read_as: Image 1: “aybreak Coffe” with text clipped at both sides.
Image 1: “esh start. Bett” clipped at both sides, followed by “coffee.” on the next line.

faults.what: The vertical version crops off both ends of the brand and headline instead of rearranging the copy to fit.
Oversized text and a large dark translucent rectangle dominate all three compositions and obscure much of the coffee cup.
The wide version crops the bottom of the cup and saucer, making the composition feel cramped.

judge.summary: Three visually consistent coffee ads are supplied, but the vertical version severely clips required copy and the layouts are cropped rather than thoughtfully rearranged.

must_haves.item: Three separate finished images are supplied, one each in 1:1, 9:16 and 16:9.
must_haves.why: Three separate outputs are visible in the requested aspect ratios.

must_haves.item: All three feature a steaming coffee cup and a consistent cream-and-dark-green palette.
must_haves.why: Each shows the same cream cup, visible steam and dark-green background.

must_haves.item: Each image contains the exact brand, headline and call to action specified.
must_haves.why: The square and wide versions contain all required copy, but the vertical version clips the brand and headline.

must_haves.item: The cup design, typography and visual styling clearly belong to the same campaign across all three images.
must_haves.why: The cup photograph, sans-serif typography, colours and dark text panel are consistent.

must_haves.item: Each layout fits its canvas without stretched imagery, clipped copy or large blank padding used merely to change the aspect ratio.
must_haves.why: The vertical layout has severe horizontal copy clipping, and the wide layout cuts off the bottom of the product composition.
